correctness.rationale: The exact family and ESI definition are specified. A selected base vertex is impossible because its pendant neighbor has no external supporter. For each selected-leaf set the zero-leaf base subset is unique, and the direct external-support condition gives exactly three local choices with polynomial weights 1, A_m and B_m. This proves all coefficients, including m=1 and disconnected/isolated graphs. For m>=2 positive top coefficients give the weighted-differential optimum and the extremizer count without cancellation; the degree threshold follows from Delta and singleton witnesses. The standalone direct checker enumerated 2,576,060 selected vertex subsets in 278 graph/multiplicity profiles, all consistent; it is finite corroboration only.

value.rationale: The complete cardinality enumerator for an arbitrary base graph leaf-corona is a natural structural refinement of the newly introduced ESI parameter, not a recomputation of a scalar known table. It identifies a sharp information contrast: the ordinary domination polynomial of a one-leaf corona ignores the base edges, whereas the ESI polynomial recovers the base domination polynomial exactly. The two-leaf invariant is exactly 2n minus the classical Roman domination number and provides a closed count of all optimal ESI sets. These are substantive connections and all-instance classifications; no general polynomial-time claim is made.
